sentence: This project studies how a part of the Lassa Virus called the fusion domain starts membrane fusion at the molecular level.
This project builds a machine learning model that predicts electron density in materials and shows how sure its predictions are.
This project makes fluorescent dyes that switch between bright, dim and dark states and uses them to study single molecules.
This project studies how eye tracking and AI can measure how engaged learners are in virtual reality training and guide their attention.
This project builds mathematical tools that use artificial neural networks to model complex systems and improve electric power distribution systems.
This project builds a software tool that uses artificial intelligence and quantum methods to help manage technical knowledge for nuclear fusion energy.
This project studies what quantum computers can and cannot do when they use only a small number of layers of operations.
This project sets up a system that separates small molecules and identifies them using liquid chromatography and mass spectrometry.
This project designs computer chips that run deep neural networks with less energy so wireless signals can be classified quickly.
This project studies how body size and genotype affect whether bumble bees spread, survive winter and cope with heat as the climate changes.
This project studies how different sugars change gene activity in bacteria and how that affects biofilm growth and makeup.
This project sets up a high-resolution mass spectrometer that can identify specific chemicals in a sample and builds labs around it.
This project improves a sandbox tool that shows virtual water flowing over sand landscapes and adds ways to model drainage and rainfall.
This project brings together hardware security researchers to discuss hardware security, including AI and quantum computing.
This project builds a cloud-based software tool that finds biomarkers to help guide lung cancer treatment decisions.
This project builds a way to image DNA inside intact cells in 3D without fluorescent labels, at extremely small length scales.
This project develops wireless systems with extremely large antenna arrays that can sense their surroundings and communicate while protecting messages from eavesdroppers.
This project applies machine learning and artificial intelligence to health problems such as emotion recognition for children with Autism Spectrum Disorder and firefighting responses.
